question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate Meta Platforms' capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, for the third quarter of 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), in US dollars, as it will be first reported in Meta's third-quarter 2026 earnings press release.

target.what: Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, as first reported by Meta Platforms, Inc. in its third-quarter 2026 earnings press release for the quarter ended 2026-09-30; consolidated worldwide, in US dollars. Working interpretation is Meta's supplemental cash-flow measure ge
target.cadence: Quarterly earnings press release; first-reported value for the quarter.
target.caveats: The cutoff date is 2026-10-19, before Meta's likely Q3 2026 earnings release, so the target is completed but not yet observable at the cutoff. The first-reported press-release figure may be rounded and may later be revised in SEC filings. The main definitional alternative is capital expenditures exc

candidates.hypothesis: The Q3 2026 first-reported value should be a continuation of Meta's recent quarterly trajectory for 'capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases'; prior quarterly levels, any seasonal or back-end-loaded ramp pattern, and FY2026 capex guidance constrain the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Meta earnings press releases and CFO commentary giving the exact line 'capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases' for Q3 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2025, Q2 2025, Q3 2025, Q4 2025, Q1 2026, and Q2 2026 if published by the cutoff; also FY2026 capex guidance/range and any Q3-specific commentary. Minimum evidence: latest four reported quarters plus guidance; substitute: 10-Q/10-K cash-flow values if press-release values are unavailable.

PP&E net, D&A, and H1 D&A are consistent with a large ongoing capex program, but they are not a direct quarterly capex estimate.

p20.role: Q3 2026 analyst consensus single-quarter capital expenditures for Meta, the same target period and entity, used as a forecast anchor before a small definition/rounding adjustment.

a1.role: dimensionless adjustment from the consensus capex measure to Meta's first-reported capex including principal payments on finance leases.

methods.rationale: Direct forecast anchor. p20 is the only Q3 2026 single-quarter capex consensus in evidence; a1 makes a small definition and rounding adjustment to Meta's including-finance-lease press-release measure. Shared dependency: p20 and p25 come from the same consensus article, so any FCF-based check would not be independent. Failure mode: consensus may be on a narrower capex definition, stale, or not fully comparable to the first-reported company measure.

p21.role: Meta H1 2026 company-measure capital expenditures including finance-lease principal, base for applying the guided H2/H1 ratio.

a2.role: dimensionless H2 2026 capex divided by H1 2026 capex, implied by the H2 capex guidance in the p21 quote.

a3.role: dimensionless Q3 2026 share of H2 2026 capex, allocating the guided H2 total to Q3.

methods.rationale: Guidance-based route. Uses H1 actual p21 and the H2 capex guide embedded in its quote: a2 converts H1 to H2, and a3 allocates H2 to Q3. Shared dependency: p21 is company-measure H1 actual while the H2 range in the quote is from a secondary article. Failure mode: Q3/Q4 timing of AI data-center and server deliveries can shift spend; if Q4 is much heavier, a3 is too high.

p67.role: Q3 2026 total revenue guidance midpoint for Meta, same quarter and company.

p1.role: Q2 2026 company-measure capex including finance-lease principal, latest actual total capex for the intensity numerator.

p47.role: Q2 2026 revenue, denominator for latest realized capex intensity.

a4.role: dimensionless Q3 2026 capex intensity uplift relative to Q2 2026 realized capex/revenue, reflecting AI infrastructure ramp and back-end-loaded spending.

methods.rationale: Revenue-guidance times latest realized capex intensity, with an uplift factor. p67 is the company Q3 revenue guidance midpoint; p1/p47 is Q2 actual total capex intensity. methods.label: m1

p20.role: Q3 2026 analyst consensus single-quarter capital expenditures for Meta, used as the direct forecast anchor.

a1.role: dimensionless adjustment from the consensus capex measure to Meta's first-reported capex including principal payments on finance leases.

methods.rationale: Direct market-consensus anchor. The main failure mode is definitional: p20 does not explicitly state whether the consensus is on Meta's including-finance-lease measure. The adjustment a1 is deliberately narrow because the finance-lease principal component is small relative to total Q2 2026 capex. This route shares the p20 dependency with the intensity and YoY routes.

methods.label: m2

p21.role: Meta H1 2026 company-measure capital expenditures including finance-lease principal, base for applying the guided H2/H1 ratio.

a2.role: dimensionless H2 2026 capex divided by H1 2026 capex, implied by the H2 capex projection in the p21 quote.

a3.role: dimensionless Q3 2026 share of H2 2026 capex, allocating the projected H2 total to Q3.

methods.rationale: Splits the H2 2026 capex projection into Q3 using H1 actual capex and the historical Q3 share of H2. The main weakness is that the H2 projection comes from the same secondary article quote as p21 and is not official guidance; p20 and p21 also share a source, so this is not fully independent of the consensus route.

methods.label: m3

p67.role: Q3 2026 total revenue guidance midpoint for Meta, same quarter and company.

p1.role: Q2 2026 company-measure capex including finance-lease principal, latest realized capex for the intensity numerator.

p47.role: Q2 2026 revenue, denominator for latest realized capex intensity.

a4.role: dimensionless Q3 2026 capex intensity uplift relative to Q2 2026 realized capex/revenue, reflecting the AI infrastructure ramp and back-end-loaded spending.

methods.rationale: Revenue-intensity route. It uses Q3 revenue guidance and the most recent realized capex intensity, then applies an explicit step-up. The key failure mode is that the implied Q3 intensity jump is large; if capex ramps less sharply than the consensus and H2 projection imply, this route overstates Q3. It indirectly depends on p20 through a4.

methods.label: m4

p163.role: Meta Q3 2025 capital expenditures including principal payments on finance leases, base for applying YoY growth.

p31.role: Q2 2026 year-over-year capex growth rate, used as a proxy for the growth rate entering Q3 2026.

a5.role: dimensionless acceleration of Q3 2026 YoY capex growth relative to the Q2 2026 YoY growth rate.

methods.rationale: YoY growth route anchored on Q3 2025 company capex. p31 is from TIKR's slightly narrower measure, but Q2 2026 company-measure growth is similar, so it is a reasonable proxy. The route assumes Q3 YoY growth accelerates from Q2; if the Q2 growth rate persists without acceleration, it will understate the consensus-implied level. It shares the p20 consensus anchor indirectly through a5.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
